podcast.title: Is my phone smarter than me?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: How many apps do you use before breakfast? Guess: who in this episode loses everything on their phone — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome back to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today we're talking about technology — and I have a sad story.
Oh no. What happened?
Last week my phone had a crash. The screen went black and it never came back. [sigh] All my photos, all my notes... gone.
Didn't you use cloud storage? Your photos can live online, not only on the phone.
I know, I know. My phone asked me again and again: 'Do you want to back up?' And I always pressed 'Later'.
[laugh] Like every update. 'Remind me tomorrow.'
Exactly! So now I'm learning. I'm trying to get up to speed with all these settings.
Good. Because phones today are amazing. Mine knows what music I like before I do.
That's the algorithm. It watches what you click and makes a guess about what you want next.
It's a little scary, isn't it? And now there's artificial intelligence in everything — my email, my camera, even my fridge!
Your fridge has AI?
Well... it tells me when the milk is finished. [chuckle] That's cutting edge for me.
[laugh] And automation is everywhere at work too. Machines do the boring jobs, so people can do the interesting ones. At least, that's the idea.
Some people worry about their jobs, though.
True. It's a big question. But let's talk about something we can all do today: cybersecurity.
Yes! My first tip: please don't use the same password for everything.
Guilty. [short pause] Mine used to be my cat's name and one, two, three.
Sam! Use a long password, like a short sentence, and turn on the second step — the code on your phone.
Okay. And my tip: if a message looks strange, don't click. Just pull the plug on the conversation.
Great advice. Now your question for your next SpeakLab call: which app could you never live without — and why?
And I'll be backing up my new phone. Every week. Promise.
[laugh] We'll check! Bye for now!

questions.q: What does an algorithm do, according to Sam?

questions.q: Leyla's fridge can order milk by itself.

questions.why: He is learning the settings he ignored before.

questions.why: "Use a long password, like a short sentence, and turn on the second step."
